subject: Setting prior scale as sigma in rstanarm

messages.author: a3e1431a16108280
messages.subject: Setting prior scale as sigma in rstanarm
parts:
I am relatively new to stan and even newer to rstanarm so my apologies for this basic question.  I am trying to build a three level model where I pool slopes at both levels but not intercepts. In stan_lmer, I haven't been able to figure out how to specify priors for the global slope. Specifically, I'd like to use sigma as my scale parameter, so maybe something like- prior=normal(0, scale=sigma)? In stan, I would have it written as: b_thirdlevel~normal(mu_b, sigma_b).

Here's my proposed model (without the global priors):

simple<-stan_lmer(y~x+(0+x|third level group/second level group), iter=3000, prior_covariance=decov(scale=10))


Any help would be much appreciated!

cheers,
Heather

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Setting prior scale as sigma in rstanarm
parts:
On Sunday, January 15, 2017 at 9:02:22 PM UTC-5, Heather wrote:
I am relatively new to stan and even newer to rstanarm so my apologies for this basic question.  I am trying to build a three level model where I pool slopes at both levels but not intercepts. In stan_lmer, I haven't been able to figure out how to specify priors for the global slope. Specifically, I'd like to use sigma as my scale parameter, so maybe something like- prior=normal(0, scale=sigma)? In stan, I would have it written as: b_thirdlevel~normal(mu_b, sigma_b).

That is not possible in rstanarm; the arguments to the function passed to the prior argument have to be constants. It might be possible in brms.

But if by sigma you mean the standard deviation of the errors in a Gaussian model, that is a weird prior belief because as sigma approaches 0, beta approaches 0, which would only work if the outcome was a constant. In Gaussian models, the normal prior on the b terms is already being scaled by sigma.


Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Setting prior scale as sigma in rstanarm
parts:
On Monday, January 16, 2017 at 4:41:13 PM UTC-5, Heather wrote:
Thanks. I meant sigma as a hierarchical sd. Is there any way to add a prior to this sigma?

Yes, specify prior_covariance = decov() with the shape and scale arguments appropriate for a gamma distribution. By default, they are both one.

Ben

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Setting prior scale as sigma in rstanarm
parts:
Hi Heather,

Just to add a bit to what Ben said, check out the vignette for stan_glmer as well as the Covariance Matrices section on the help("priors") page. The decov function Ben mentioned implements the prior described in those two spots. If you have questions about those explanations after reading them let us know (it's a bit of a novel prior but we like it a lot -- definitely an improvement on the traditional priors used for these models -- and even the default settings are pretty good in most cases).

Jonah
